releases.notes: Supplied deployment pack: 17 events, master plus 12 split calendars. Structural validation passed 17 of 17.
Portal build 1. CR-001 neutral EA milestone; CR-002 AiG deadline held as candidate; categories exported as lists (D18); personal data removed.

Owner approved CR-001, CR-002 and CR-003. EA 22 Oct is the shortlist announcement. AiG deadline released with its own split calendar. Continuity owners assigned by role. Adds planner, route finder, source registry, traceability, search and accessibility testing.

Workflows section with a declarative engine: nominate (7 gated steps to a submission pack), thank, credit, MoG handover (meets FR-08), change request and source re-verification. AI throughout: an agentic portal assistant, draft from evidence, tighten, and an agentic criteria reviewer whose edits need acceptance, all under published rules with template fallbacks. Search ranks results and hands off to the assistant. Real downloads for packs and a zipped calendar set. New icon system. Calendar content unchanged from .3.

Operating guidance (purpose, trigger, cadence, service level, done criteria, RACI, pitfalls) on every workflow. 14 more workflows: weekly triage, monthly assurance, opt-in invitation, correction and withdrawal, moderation and appeal, discovery-method check, publication clearance, calendar release, open recognition call, leaver check, in-year reward proposal, reward fairness review, personal evidence builder, objectives and PDP. Operating rhythm with due dates and a calendar export; My work dashboard. New Recognition section: 33 ways to recognise including pay and reward (checked against the 2026 to 2027 pay remit guidance and HMRC rules), role pages for peers, line managers, leaders and HR, and person-controlled links to objectives, development plans, reviews and Success Profiles. The assistant can recommend and start workflows. Ethical proportionality: ten ways of weighing effort assessed (hours and popularity rejected), a contribution rubric guide with bands, legal anchors, and a band field in the reward proposal. Help section: user guide, five guided tours, four self-checking tutorials with knowledge checks, and a shared idea box with votes and a wishlist from the build. Benefits and schemes page linking official Civil Service pay, pension, terms, wellbeing and benefits sources. Inclusive design: display and access settings (text size, easier reading spacing, high contrast, reduced motion, underlined links, Easy Read and text-only modes), Easy Read page, one-page text-only version, draft accessibility statement, top-task entry points, breadcrumbs, on-this-page links, previous and next signposts, reading time, automatic glossary tooltips, chart text alternatives, page feedback, and inclusive-language, plain-English and accessible-name self-checks. Calendar content unchanged.

New Connect section: send recognition to Microsoft Teams (chat deep link, Praise, meeting form, Workflows Adaptive Cards), Outlook, Viva Engage, Gmail and Google Calendar (live through the viewer's own claude.ai connectors, drafts only), Google Chat, Slack (mrkdwn, Block Kit, Workflow Builder), Zoom, Webex, Atlassian, Notion, any email or calendar app, and Open Badges 3.0, with an integration register of 27 entries, ten integration rules, admin recipes and a Request an integration workflow. A Send button under every workflow output with a privacy check and a confirmation tick. Colour system with eight accessible hues per section and card, an icon on every card and panel, a tab scroller, a site map with recently viewed pages, a footer site map, print styles and an overflow guard checked at seven screen widths. Recognition section adds Innovation (15 mechanisms, seven principles and routes for nine profession groups including digital, data, technology and cyber), Public sector schemes (20 schemes across central, local and devolved government and the wider public sector, each with dates and basis, including the Civil Service AI & Data Challenge and the Cabinet Secretary's AI Innovation Award) and Missions and priorities (eight possible links assessed, with conditions on impartiality, devolution, age and pay). Self-checks K35 to K40. Defects D23 to D25 fixed. Calendar content unchanged; CR-004 proposed for new scheme dates.

CR-004 approved and released: nine public sector scheme events (iESE 2027 deadline; LGC 2027 shortlist; LGC, MJ, iESE, HSJ and Scottish Public Service Awards ceremonies; watch markers for the Civil Service AI & Data Challenge and the Cabinet Secretary's AI Innovation Award), seven route split calendars and a Public sector schemes split. CR-005: verification note on the Civil Service Awards deadline. Seven new routes in the route register and source registry. Further improvements listed in the release notes for this build.

New front page with a liquid glass, fluid design: an original logo, a once-per-session splash screen, a hero, a quick launch bar and a pausable highlights carousel built from verified content and live calendar data. Spotlight and profiles: 70 publicly announced winners from organiser and official pages (individuals, teams and organisations, each with its source), network profiles from the register, and opt-in profiles that people add and remove themselves. Media centre with the logo, palette, a banner maker (PNG and SVG), a comms toolkit and media guidance. Quick actions menu on every page. Recognition domains: 20 domains from cross-government join-up and data sharing to maintenance, with incentives for individuals, teams and organisations and published examples. Alerts and subscriptions: follow routes and event types, choose reminder times, a personal subscription calendar with reminders, a notifications centre with unread badge, personal reminders, a weekly digest to share, Google Calendar reminders through the viewer's connector, and browser notifications where allowed. The front page flags every deadline in the next 60 days by urgency, with an alert bar when one is within 7 days. Self-checks K42 to K48.

Information architecture restructure: nine sections in order of importance (Home, Workflows, Recognition, Calendar, Awards, Connect, Evidence, Help, Build hub); North Star, What it is not and Theory of change merged into About the portfolio; This fortnight merged into the agenda and front page; Register and Safeguards merged into Evidence; glossary and sources moved to Help; specialist content (releases, change control, architecture, service design, governance, data standards, assurance) moved to a new Build hub; 44 old addresses redirect (K49). Masthead: search bar, Quick launch anchored under the masthead (no duplicate Ask), notifications, and one Settings panel for theme, text size, access, layout, help and portal health; the bottom-right corner is only for Ask. Pages menu collapses to an icon rail on wide screens and opens off-canvas on phones. Plain-language What's new. Splash screen with what closes next, four ways in and the latest news, under the person's control. Favicon from the logo. Brand kit and style guide with logo variants, colour contrast table, type, icons, components, voice, certificate template, and a 16-slide brand deck to present, print or download. Information architecture review page. GitHub repository with Pages, issue forms for ideas, bugs, corrections and date changes linked from the idea box, footer and settings, and scheduled source, staleness, link and digest checks; calendar subscription by link.

Professional review in the Build hub: the Hub and its build process assessed from the viewpoint of 20 professions (service owner to finance), each with strengths, concerns, a rating and owned actions grounded in measured evidence; the build process against the GDS lifecycle and the 14 Service Standard points (self-assessed); an adversarial view of ten arguments against the Hub with responses and verdicts, six abuse cases, and the ten actions that matter most. Self-check K50. Calendar content unchanged.

Acting on the professional review. Security: a Content Security Policy that allows only this build's own scripts (by hash), fonts and styles on the GitHub Pages build; fonts hosted with the site; hostile ideas and profiles tested so no markup or script runs and no assistant tool returns shared text. Governance drafts for sign-off: DPIA screening, privacy notice, Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard screening, success measures with a measured freshness baseline, core tasks, research plan and a modelled maintenance estimate. Proposed page owners and review dates on every page; assumption labels on untested journey and role pages; a department policy caveat on every financial method; Not an official announcement on generated banners; Open Government Licence and official address in the footer. Engineering: source split into ordered files with no copies, ESLint, unit tests for tools, keyboard tests, waits for render instead of fixed waits on navigation, a Firefox and WebKit smoke job, fork pull requests that build without the name list, an uptime check and a branch protection script. ADR-08 to ADR-10. Self-checks K51 to K53. Calendar content unchanged.

Full data protection impact assessment following the ICO's seven steps: 12 kinds of data, 13 risks rated before and after measures (none high afterwards, so no ICO prior consultation), lawful bases, retention, rights and transfers, with sign-off for the DPO and information asset owner. Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard: not required, with the tests, reasons and triggers to revisit, and a voluntary AI transparency statement. Standards and frameworks register of 17 items, with point-by-point assessments against the Technology Code of Practice, Secure by Design, the AI Playbook for the UK Government and the Data and AI Ethics Framework, and an equality impact screening. New Help page, Privacy and your data: the privacy notice, every item kept in the browser with the rule it relies on, a clear-all control and an opt-out from remembering pages. Profiles are hidden 12 months after their last update. AI notice to follow departmental policy. Self-checks K55 to K57. Calendar content unchanged.

Executing on the DPIA and standards findings. Data quality scorecard measuring the six dimensions of the Government Data Quality Framework on every build, with an action plan against its five principles (K58); accuracy is 72% because five sources are unverified. Security risk assessment of ten threats scored before and after controls (K59), and the uptime check now confirms the live page keeps its security policy. Record of processing under Article 30. Published winners kept for the last three award years (K60). New WCAG 2.2 tests for text spacing, focus not obscured, forced colours and reduced motion; they found that search results stayed open over the page after focus moved on (D36) and that the Ask button could cover a focused link (D37), both fixed. One search ranking for the masthead and the assistant, with a 23-case evaluation set run on every change. Accessibility statement now lists the testing done. Defects D35 to D37. Calendar content unchanged.

Source re-verification on 19 Oct 2026. National Diversity Awards: no 2027 dates published yet. UK Honours: process, confidentiality (do not tell the nominee), two supporting letters from people who know the nominee, individuals only, and the GOV.UK timescale now verified on official pages. King's Award for Voluntary Service: KAVS 2027 nominations close on 1 December 2026 and eligibility is confirmed on the DCMS site; the deadline is proposed as CR-006 and held as a candidate until approved. Cabinet Secretary's AI Innovation Award: official launch message now the source; quarterly, individuals and teams, prizes confirmed; the form is closed and the next window is not published. Diversity UK: recipients are chosen by its trustees, so it is not an open nomination route. A duplicate registry row for the AI Innovation Award was removed (D39) and the data quality check now catches duplicate registry rows. Data quality accuracy rises from 72% to 100%.

CR-006 approved by the service owner and released: King's Award for Voluntary Service 2027 nominations close on 1 December 2026, with reminders 14 and 3 days before, in the Deadlines and UK Honours calendars. CR-007: the National Diversity Awards 2026 shortlist was in July (organiser timeline), not 24 June as the pack said. Fact-level verification: 13 more route facts checked against organiser pages (Civil Service Awards format, self-nomination and categories; British Diversity Awards categories; Ethnicity Awards evidence window; National Diversity Awards timeline and categories; Analysis in Government categories). Portfolio operating rules are now labelled O instead of being counted as unverified facts. One fact remains unconfirmed: whether self-nomination is allowed for the Cabinet Secretary's AI Innovation Award, which can only be checked when its form reopens. Accuracy now counts facts as well as sources: 98.2%. Engineering close-out: the application runs in one function scope so nothing leaks onto the page's global object; every fixed wait in the tests is replaced by a condition; every GitHub Action is pinned to a commit hash and the configuration check enforces it.

The service owner confirmed that self-nomination is allowed for the Cabinet Secretary's AI Innovation Award. No public page states it and the nomination form is closed, so the fact carries a new provenance code, S (confirmed by the service owner), and should be rechecked against the form when it reopens. All 38 organiser facts and 17 sources are now confirmed: data quality accuracy is 100%.

New page: Awards › Community and heritage. Nine routes that recognise Black, African, Caribbean and Mixed people and communities (UK honours, the Windrush Day Grant Scheme, National Lottery Heritage Grants, English Heritage blue plaques, Nubian Jak plaques, the MOBO Awards, the Powerlist, the Black British Business Awards and the NHS Windrush 70 Awards as a past example), and the Cabinet Office's published figures on Black and Mixed honours recipients for six lists from June 2019 to December 2024, with the 2021 Census baseline. Every fact was re-read on its source page on 25 October 2026; one route is marked L (press report). Seven sources added (S78 to S84). New self-check K61 with a deliberate-break test. A See also link points to the BHM 2026 Hub. Calendar events, the data build date and organiser verification dates are unchanged. The release identifier hash is now the SHA-256 of the Hub data block.

Renamed the Awards and Recognition Hub (formerly the Recognition Opportunities Portal); page addresses, saved settings and calendar UIDs are unchanged, so subscriptions keep working. All 17 organiser sources re-read on 22 November 2026: 16 confirmed and the Ethnicity Awards page could not be read (bot check), so it is marked not re-verified. New deadline: the Civil Service AI & Data Challenge 2026 to 2027 closes on 10 December 2026 (CR-008). Release codes are now generated by the build from the data, two new self-checks (K62 old name, K63 release codes) with deliberate-break tests, and the source now lives in a public GitHub repository with Pages hosting.
